prompt: Another app on the same phone tries to open the planner's planner.db. What happens?

choices.text: It opens it, because both apps belong to the same user
choices.why: On a phone the boundary is the app, not the user.

choices.text: It opens it read-only
choices.why: There is no read-only exception for another app's sandbox.

choices.text: It cannot
choices.why: Right. The file is in the planner's sandbox, and other apps cannot access it.

choices.text: The system asks the user for a storage permission first
choices.why: No permission opens another app's sandbox.

prompt: A student exports her study plan as a PDF and expects to keep it after deleting the planner. Where must the app put the PDF?

choices.text: In shared storage, through the system's picker
choices.why: Right. Uninstalling removes the sandbox; shared storage stays.

choices.text: In the cache, so it does not take up space
choices.why: The cache goes with the app, and may go sooner.

choices.text: In the app's files folder, which is backed up
choices.why: Backed up or not, the sandbox goes with the app.

choices.text: In the Keychain
choices.why: The Keychain is for small secrets, not documents.

prompt: The planner keeps the study plan in the cache folder, and it works through every test. What goes wrong, and when?

choices.text: The plan is copied to every backup twice
choices.why: The cache is left out of backups, not doubled.

choices.text: Nothing: the cache is a folder like any other
choices.why: The system may delete it on its own, which no other folder allows.

choices.text: The app crashes on start
choices.why: It starts fine, with an empty plan, which is worse.

choices.text: When the disk is nearly full, the system clears the cache and the plan is empty
choices.why: Right. Nothing fails; the plan just looks like one nobody wrote.

prompt: Which of these are true of an app's sandbox, on both platforms? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Other apps cannot read it
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: It is removed when the app is uninstalled
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Part of it may be emptied by the system
choices.why: Right: the cache.

choices.text: Everything in it is encrypted
choices.why: The sandbox keeps other apps out; it does not encrypt your files.

prompt: Which question decides whether a file belongs in the cache?

choices.text: Is it larger than 1 MB?
choices.why: Size does not decide it; a small plan is still the student's data.

choices.text: Could the app make it again?
choices.why: Right. If yes, the system may delete it and nothing is lost.

choices.text: Does the user need to see it in a file manager?
choices.why: That decides Documents against Application Support, not the cache.

choices.text: Was it written in the last 24 hours?
choices.why: Age has nothing to do with it.

prompt: Match each iOS folder to the Android folder that makes the same promise.
According to Android's Auto Backup guide, how many megabytes of backup data may each app have?
A student moves to a new phone and restores her backup. Which of the planner's files should not come with her?

choices.text: planner.db, because a database cannot be restored
choices.why: It is restored like any file, and it is exactly what she wants back.

choices.text: The push token issued for the old phone
choices.why: Right. It identifies the old device; Android's guide says a restored one can make the app misbehave.

choices.text: prefs.json, because settings belong to a device
choices.why: A tab and a theme are hers, and coming back with them is a kindness.

choices.text: None: a backup should bring everything back
choices.why: A device-specific identifier must not travel.

prompt: Which iOS folders does iCloud Backup leave out by default?

choices.text: Documents and Library
choices.why: Both are backed up, apart from Library/Caches.

choices.text: None: iCloud backs up the whole container
choices.why: Caches and tmp are excluded.

choices.text: Application Support and tmp
choices.why: Application Support is backed up.

choices.text: Library/Caches and tmp
choices.why: Right. The system purges them, so the backup skips them.

prompt: Why is a preferences store the wrong place for the planner's sessions?

choices.text: It is read and written whole, with no queries, and sessions grow every week
choices.why: Right. It is built for a handful of settings read at start.

choices.text: Preferences are deleted when the phone restarts
choices.why: They persist; that is their point.

choices.text: Preferences cannot hold numbers
choices.why: They hold numbers; that is not the problem.

choices.text: Other apps can read preferences
choices.why: They are in the sandbox like everything else.

prompt: prefs.ts writes prefs.json.tmp and then renames it. What does that protect against?

choices.text: The backup copying an old version
choices.why: The backup is not what the rename is for.

choices.text: Another app reading the settings
choices.why: The sandbox does that; the rename is about crashes.

choices.text: A half-written file if the process dies mid-write
choices.why: Right. The rename is one step: the old file or the new one, never half of each.

choices.text: Two settings with the same name
choices.why: A JSON object cannot hold two of the same key anyway.

prompt: Version 2 of the planner adds a setting, fontSize, with a default of 16. A student upgrades from version 1, whose prefs.json has only tab and theme. With load() as written, what does she get for fontSize?

choices.why: Right. Defaults first, then whatever the file has on top.

choices.text: undefined, because the file does not mention it
choices.why: The defaults are spread first, so the missing key keeps its default.

choices.text: An error, because the file is from an older version
choices.why: Nothing checks a version; the merge handles it.

choices.text: The defaults for every setting, throwing away her theme
choices.why: Her theme is in the file, and the file wins over the defaults.

prompt: How many bytes did prefs.json take after the two changes in the lesson?
On iOS, small settings are kept with ___; on Android, with DataStore.
What is SQLite, as a phone uses it?

choices.text: A database server the app connects to over the network
choices.why: It is not a server at all.

choices.text: Android's version of Room
choices.why: Room is a layer over SQLite.

choices.text: A library that keeps a whole database in one file
choices.why: Right, and it ships inside both Android and iOS.

choices.text: A file format only iOS can read
choices.why: Both platforms ship it.

prompt: Why does running store.ts a second time leave the totals at 180 and 120?

choices.text: Because the database is recreated empty each time
choices.why: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS keeps what is there.

choices.text: INSERT OR IGNORE skips rows whose id exists
choices.why: Right. The ids are the primary keys, so the second run adds nothing.

choices.text: Because the transaction is rolled back the second time
choices.why: Nothing is rolled back; nothing new is written.

choices.text: Because SUM ignores duplicate rows
choices.why: SUM adds every row it is given; there are no duplicates to give it.

prompt: planner.db was 20,480 bytes in pages of 4,096. How many pages is that?
Version 2 of the planner adds a notes column to sessions. What must it do on phones that already hold version 1's database?

choices.text: Nothing: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS adds the column
choices.why: It does nothing when the table exists, so the old table stays as it was.

choices.text: Delete planner.db and start again
choices.why: That throws away every session the student wrote.

choices.text: Ask the student to reinstall the app
choices.why: Reinstalling deletes the sandbox, and the data with it.

choices.text: Migrate the table in place, keeping every row
choices.why: Right. A migration, on a device nobody can log into.

prompt: Match each platform to the layer the courses after the fork put over its storage.
Why does the sign-in token not belong in preferences?

choices.text: Other apps read preferences
choices.why: The sandbox keeps them out; that part is fine.

choices.text: Preferences cannot hold long strings
choices.why: Length is not the problem.

choices.text: They are stored unencrypted, and backed up
choices.why: Right. Apple's documentation says exactly that, and points at the Keychain.

choices.text: The token would be lost when the app closes
choices.why: Preferences persist; the problem is who else could read them.

prompt: What does the Android Keystore hold, unlike the iOS Keychain?

choices.text: A key whose bytes never reach the app
choices.why: Right. The key encrypts the token inside the Keystore; the result can sit in a file.

choices.text: The secret itself, encrypted
choices.why: That is the Keychain's shape.

choices.text: The user's password, in plain text
choices.why: Nothing in it is plain text.

choices.text: A copy of the app's preferences
choices.why: Preferences are a separate, unencrypted store.

prompt: A developer stores a payment provider's private API key in the Keychain at first launch, copying it from a constant in the app's code. What has this achieved?

choices.text: The key is now safe, because the Keychain is encrypted
choices.why: It was already readable in the app itself, in every copy.

choices.text: The key moves to the server on first launch
choices.why: Nothing moves it; it should have lived there from the start.

choices.text: The key can no longer be extracted from the app
choices.why: The constant is still in the code.

choices.text: Nothing: the key is in every copy of the app already
choices.why: Right. A secret shipped inside the app is not a secret; it belongs on the server.

prompt: On iOS, a student uninstalls the planner and installs it again. What may she find, according to expo-secure-store's documentation?

choices.text: Her whole planner.db, restored from the sandbox
choices.why: The sandbox went with the app.

choices.text: The token from before, still in the Keychain
choices.why: Right. Keychain items may survive an uninstall, and an app should not rely on either outcome.

choices.text: Her preferences, kept by UserDefaults
choices.why: UserDefaults lives in the sandbox and goes with it.

choices.text: Nothing at all, guaranteed
choices.why: The documentation says the opposite can happen.
